title: Pulmonology Language Access: A Clinical Workflow
summary: Improve pulmonology language access for symptom histories, pulmonary function testing, inhaler teaching, action plans, and follow-up.
body_markdown:
###


Record preferred spoken and written languages, dialect when relevant, safe contact method, interpretation preference, test preparation needs, and any communication accommodation. Route the information to every team involved.


###


The technologist should demonstrate the maneuver and use short, consistent, timed commands. Confirm understanding before recording, avoid overlapping speech, and document communication issues separately from maneuver quality.


###


Use the exact prescribed device, demonstrate each step, and ask the patient to perform the full sequence. Verify the medicine, purpose, dose, timing, cleaning, and missed-dose plan.


###


The translated plan should match current clinician orders and state medicines, triggers, worsening signs, actions, contact information, and when to seek urgent or emergency care.


###


Yes, with clear audio, respiratory terminology, verification of numbers and negation, device return demonstration, teach-back, documentation, and another option when patient preference, policy, or encounter needs call for it.
